title: A passage a day
note: Written by hand, verified against data/book.json by tools/build-daily.js. Each quote must appear in the book exactly once, word for word; the build refuses anything it cannot find or finds twice, and the text that ships is the book's own, copied out of book.json rather than out of this file.

passages.quote: The only requirement for membership is an honest desire to stop drinking.
In nearly all cases, their ideals must be grounded in a power greater than themselves, if they are to re-create their lives.

They are restless, irritable and discontented, unless they can again experience the sense of ease and comfort which comes at once by taking a few drinks–drinks which they see others taking with impunity.
I earnestly advise every alcoholic to read this book through, and though perhaps he came to scoff, he may remain to pray.
I was to know happiness, peace, and usefulness, in a way of life that is incredibly more wonderful as time passes.
Never mind the musty past; here sat a miracle directly across the kitchen table.
It was only a matter of being willing to believe in a power greater than myself.
Upon a foundation of complete willingness I might build what I saw in my friend.
There was a sense of victory, followed by such a peace and serenity as I had never known.
I felt lifted up, as though the great clean wind of a mountain top blew through and through.
Never was I to pray for myself, except as my requests bore on my usefulness to others.
I soon found that when all other measures failed, work with another alcoholic would save the day.
Faith has to work twenty-four hours a day in and through us, or we perish.
Each day my friend’s simple talk in our kitchen multiplies itself in a widening circle of peace on earth and good will to men.
But there exists among us a fellowship, a friendliness, and an understanding which is indescribably wonderful.
The feeling of having shared in a common peril is one element in the powerful cement which binds us.
The tremendous fact for every one of us is that we have discovered a common solution.
Our very lives, as ex-alcoholics, depend upon our constant thought of others and how we may help meet their needs.
When, therefore, we were approached by those in whom the problem had been solved, there was nothing left for us but to pick up the simple kit of spiritual tools laid at our feet.
We have found much of heaven and we have been rocketed into a fourth dimension of existence, of which we had not even dreamed.
What seemed at first a flimsy reed, has proved to be the loving and powerful hand of God.
We learned that we had to fully concede to our innermost selves that we were alcoholics.
The delusion that we are like other people, or presently may be, has to be smashed.
My old manner of life was by no means a bad one, but I would not exchange its best moments for the worst I have now.
Most alcoholics have to be pretty badly mangled before they really commence to solve their problems.
We had to find a power by which we could live, and it had to be A Power Greater Than Ourselves.
We found that God does not make too hard terms with those who seek Him.
To us, the Realm of Spirit is broad, roomy, all inclusive; never exclusive or forbidding, to those who earnestly seek.
When, therefore, we speak to you of God, we mean your own conception of God.
It has been repeatedly proven among us that upon this simple cornerstone a wonderfully effective spiritual structure can be built.
We missed the reality and the beauty of the forest because we were diverted by the ugliness of some of its trees.
The outlines and the promise of the New Land had brought lustre to tired eyes and fresh courage to flagging spirits.
So, in one way or another, we discovered that faith had been involved all the time!
We finally saw that faith in some kind of God was a part of our make-up, just as much as the feeling we have for a friend.
Rarely have we seen a person fail who has thoroughly followed our path.
We thought we could find an easier, softer way. But we could not.
With all the earnestness at our command, we beg of you to be fearless and thorough from the very start.
Some of us have tried to hold on to our old ideas and the result was nil until we let go absolutely.
Each person is like an actor who wants to run the whole show: is forever trying to arrange the lights, the ballet, the scenery and the rest of the players in his own way.
Driven by a hundred forms of fear, self-delusion, self-seeking, and self-pity, we step on the toes of our fellows and they retaliate.
Most good ideas are simple and this concept was the keystone of the new and triumphant arch through which we passed to freedom.
More and more we became interested in seeing what we could contribute to life.
Taking a commercial inventory is a fact-finding and a fact-facing process.
For when harboring such feelings we shut ourselves off from the sunlight of the Spirit.
We asked God to help us show them the same tolerance, pity, and patience that we would cheerfully grant a sick friend.
Putting out of our minds the wrongs others had done, we resolutely looked for our own mistakes.
Just to the extent that we do as we think He would have us, and humbly rely on Him, does He enable us to match calamity with serenity.
Whatever our ideal turns out to be, we must be willing to grow toward it.
In this book you read again and again that faith did for us what we could not do for ourselves.
They took inventory all right, but hung on to some of the worst items in stock.
We must be entirely honest with somebody if we expect to live long or happily in this world.
The rule is we must be hard on ourself, but always considerate of others.
We pocket our pride and go to it, illuminating every twist of character, every dark cranny of the past.
Our real purpose is to fit ourselves to be of maximum service to God and the people about us.
It is harder to go to an enemy than to a friend, but we find it much more beneficial to us.
We are there to sweep off our side of the street, realizing that nothing worth while can be accomplished until we do so, never trying to tell him what he should do.
Sometimes the man we are calling upon admits his own fault; so feuds of years’ standing melt away in an hour.
So we clean house with the family, asking each morning in meditation that our Creator show us the way of patience, tolerance, kindliness and love.
We are going to know a new freedom and happiness. We will not regret the past nor wish to shut the door on it. We will comprehend the word serenity and know peace.
No matter how far down the scale we have gone, we will see how our experience can benefit others.
We will lose interest in selfish things and gain interest in our fellows.
What we really have is a daily reprieve contingent on the maintenance of our spiritual condition.
Every day is a day when we must carry the vision of God’s will into all of our activities.
Or were we thinking of what we could do for others, of what we could pack into the stream of life?
Our thought life will be placed on a much higher plane when our thinking is cleared of wrong motives.
As we go through the day, we pause when agitated or doubtful, and ask for the right thought or action.
Practical experience shows that nothing will so much insure immunity from drinking as intensive work with other alcoholics.
To watch people recover, to see them help others, to watch loneliness vanish, to see a fellowship grow up about you, to have a host of friends–this is an experience you must not miss.
Frequent contact with newcomers and with each other is the bright spot of our lives.
To be vital, faith must be accompanied by self sacrifice and unselfish, constructive action.
Never talk down to an alcoholic from any moral or spiritual hilltop, simply lay out the kit of spiritual tools for his inspection.
We have no monopoly on God; we merely have an approach that worked with us.
Both you and the new man must walk day by day in the path of spiritual progress.
When we look back, we realize that the things which came to us when we put ourselves in God’s hands were better than anything we could have planned.
Keep on the firing line of life with these motives, and God will keep you unharmed.
We grow by our willingness to face and rectify errors and convert them into assets.
Cling to the thought that, in God’s hands, the dark past is the greatest possession you have–the key to life and happiness for others.
For us, material well-being always followed spiritual progress; it never preceded.
We have come to believe He would like us to keep our heads in the clouds with Him, but that our feet ought to be firmly planted on earth, nevertheless.
We have found nothing incompatible between a powerful spiritual experience, and a life of sane and happy usefulness.
If newcomers could see no joy or fun in our existence, they wouldn’t want it.
We are sure God wants us to be happy, joyous, and free.
But it is clear that we made our own misery. God didn’t do it.
As we became subjects of King Alcohol, shivering denizens of his mad realm, the chilling vapor that is loneliness settled down.
You will be bound to them with new and wonderful ties, for you will escape disaster together and you will commence shoulder to shoulder your common journey.
Then you will know what it means to give of yourself, that others may survive and rediscover life.
The practical answer is that since these things have happened among us, they can happen with you.
It was transcended by the happiness they found in giving themselves for others.
No one is too discredited, nor has sunk too low to be welcomed cordially–if he means business.
And so can you, though you be but one man with this book in your hand.
Ask him in your morning meditation what you can do each day for the man who is still sick.
See to it that your relationship with Him is right, and great events will come to pass for you and countless others.
Abandon yourself to God as you understand God. Admit your faults to him and your fellows. Clear away the wreckage of your past. Give freely of what you find, and join us.
We shall be with you, in the Fellowship of The Spirit, and you will surely meet some of us as you trudge the Road of Happy Destiny.

cravingNote: Shown on the craving screen, one at a time. Weighted towards what to do rather than what is wrong with you — someone reading this is in the middle of it, not studying it. A passage may appear in both lists; the book only says a thing once and the two lists are read in different moods.

craving.quote: All these, and many others, have one symptom in common: they cannot start drinking without developing the phenomenon of craving.
These men were not drinking to escape; they were drinking to overcome a craving beyond their mental control.
There is a complete failure of the kind of defense that keeps one from putting his hand on a hot stove.
But there was always the curious mental phenomenon, that parallel with our sound reasoning there inevitably ran some insanely trivial excuse for taking the first drink.

Once more: the alcoholic at certain times has no effective mental defense against the first drink. Except in a few rare cases, neither he nor any other human being can provide such a defense. His defense must come from a higher Power.
As we go through the day, we pause when agitated or doubtful, and ask for the right thought or action.
Do not think of what you will get out of the occasion. Think of what you can bring to it. But if you are shaky, you had better work with another alcoholic instead!
Many times I have gone to my old hospital in despair. On talking to a man there, I would be amazingly lifted up and set on my feet. It is a design for living that works in rough going.
We ask Him to remove our fear and direct our attention to what He would have us be. At once, we commence to outgrow fear.
Practical experience shows that nothing will so much insure immunity from drinking as intensive work with other alcoholics.
What we really have is a daily reprieve contingent on the maintenance of our spiritual condition.
